properties.areaDesc: Coastal waters from  Suwannee River to Keaton Beach out 20 NM; Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued July 31 at 9:40AM EDT until July 31 at 11:15AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from  Suwannee River to Keaton Beach out 20 NM...
Waters from Suwannee River to Apalachicola FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 1115 AM EDT.

* At 940 AM EDT, severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from 16 nm
southeast of Buckeye Reef to near Suwannee River, moving southeast
at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts 34 knots or greater, and small
hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Horseshoe Beach and Suwannee River.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 31 at 8:04AM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Major flooding is forecast.

- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 39.2 feet
just after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 30 at 9:55PM CDT until July 31 at 10:00AM CDT by NWS Aberdeen SD
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northwestern Day County in northeastern South Dakota...

* WHEN...Until 1000 AM CDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. It will take
several hours for all the water from these storms to work through
local drainage systems in urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 953 PM CDT, emergency management reported heavy rain in the
warned area due to thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing. Between 4
and 8 inches of rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Roslyn and Pierpont.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.areaDesc: Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Pensacola FL from 20 to 60 NM
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued July 31 at 9:41AM CDT until July 31 at 11:15AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
SMWMOB

The National Weather Service in Mobile has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Pensacola FL from 20 to
60 NM...

* Until 1115 AM CDT.

* At 941 AM CDT, a strong thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 9 nm south of Oriskany Reef, or 28 nm
southeast of Pensacola Pass. The strong thunderstorm was nearly
stationary.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.areaDesc: Le Sueur, MN; Nicollet, MN; Sibley, MN
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 31 at 7:52AM CDT until July 31 at 1:45PM CDT by NWS Twin Cities/Chanhassen MN
properties.description:
FFWMPX

The National Weather Service in the Twin Cities has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Sibley County in central Minnesota...
Central Le Sueur County in south central Minnesota...
Northeastern Nicollet County in south central Minnesota...

* Until 145 PM CDT.

* At 752 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 3.5 and 4.5 inches of
rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...The pubic reported over 4 inches of rain fell in some
spots, and radar indicated additional rainfall of 1 to 3
inches possible this morning.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
St. Peter, Le Sueur, Le Center, Henderson, Kasota, Ottawa, St
Thomas and St Henry.
